column2: description
Description or code for the mechanism that ended the test, such as local buckling, screw pull-over, panel tearing or yielding.

column1: Failure line load per purlin line
column2: The maximum uniform load per foot carried by a single purlin or girt line at failure of the full-scale assembly, the headline strength result of each uplift test.
The bending moment in the member at failure, computed from the measured failure load and span, used to compare with code bending capacities.
The uniform suction pressure applied by the vacuum chamber at failure (or at each recorded load stage), before conversion to a line load on the member.
column32: failure_load_as_printed, vacuum_pressure_in_water [psf / in. of water check]

column2: Stiffness of the panel-to-purlin connection against rotation of the member, measured in companion F-tests and used in lateral-torsional strength models.
Measured lateral (horizontal) movement of the purlin web or compression flange during loading, showing how much the unbraced member drifted sideways.
Measured vertical (downward or upward) deflection of the test member under load, typically at midspan of the critical bay.
Rotation (twist) of the purlin cross-section under load, measured from paired dial gage displacements, indicating torsional response of the unbraced member.
Longitudinal inward movement of the end supports during the test, checked to confirm catenary (membrane) forces were relieved.
Distance from the observed buckle or failure location to the nearest support or to midspan, recording where the member failed.
Load carried by an individual through-fastening screw at failure or at a load stage, measuring the pullover strength of the panel-to-purlin connection.
Stress in the member computed from strain gage readings at a given load, used to track how the section is stressed before failure.
Raw strain gage readings taken on the member or panel at each applied load level.
Yield stress of the member steel measured on tensile coupons, the material property that sets the fully-yielded bending capacity.
Percent elongation of the tensile coupon at fracture, a measure of steel ductility.
Ultimate tensile strength of the steel measured on tensile coupons, reported alongside yield stress.
Elastic modulus of the steel assumed or input in the stress and section-property calculations.
Yield stress of the roof or wall panel sheet steel, distinct from the purlin steel, affecting panel bending and fastener pullover.
Base (uncoated) steel thickness of the cold-formed purlin or girt, the dominant parameter for local buckling and strength.
Overall out-to-out web depth of the purlin or girt cross-section, the key geometric property controlling bending stiffness.
Shape of the cold-formed member cross-section, C (Cee) or Z (Zee), which governs its torsional behaviour under uplift.
On-center spacing of the parallel purlin or girt lines in the test assembly, which also sets the tributary width of the applied pressure.
Width of the purlin or girt flange, reported separately for the compression (free) and tension (panel-attached) flanges.
Length of the edge stiffener (lip) on the flange, which controls distortional buckling of the compression flange.
Inside bend radius at the web-to-flange and flange-to-lip corners of the cold-formed section.
Angle between the flange and its stiffening lip, affecting the effectiveness of the edge stiffener.
Initial lateral out-of-straightness (sweep) of the member measured before loading, an imperfection that reduces uplift capacity.
Plan width of roof carried by each purlin line, used to convert the measured chamber pressure into a line load on the member.
Effective section modulus of the cold-formed section computed by effective-width analysis, used with the yield stress to give the fully braced bending capacity.
Distance from the screw centreline to the pivot corner of the fastened flange, a geometric parameter that controls the rotational restraint of the girt.

column1: Section moment of inertia and area
column2: Gross and effective moments of inertia and gross section moduli of the cross-section computed from measured dimensions, used in deflection and strength calculations.
column35: i_gross_in4, i_strength_in4, i_defl_in4, s_t_gross_in3, s_b_gross_in3 [in^4 / in^3 check]
column42: ix_in4, iy_in4, ixy_in4, ieff_in4, ag_in2 [in^4 / in^2 check]

column2: Dimensions of the panel rib profile (height, half-width, web projection and slant length) used in the biaxial membrane pullover theory.
column43: rib_height_in, rib_top_half_width_in, web_horizontal_projection_in, web_slant_length_in, l_o_in, delta_max_in

column2: Actual and code-required moments of inertia of the lip edge stiffener, checked to confirm the flange is adequately stiffened.
Measured angle between the web and the flange of the formed section, a shape imperfection affecting section properties.
Ratio of the measured failure load or moment to the capacity predicted by a code or analytical method, the headline measure of how well predictions match tests.
Mean and dispersion of the strength reduction factor R across a group of tests, used to recommend a code value.
Ratio of lap length at the interior support to the purlin depth, a design parameter for continuous lapped systems.
Ratio of model-predicted panel-to-girt rotational stiffness to the measured F-test stiffness, expressed as a percentage.

column1: Test stress as percent of yield
column2: Ultimate stress reached in the test expressed as a percentage of the coupon yield stress, showing how close the section came to yielding.
Fraction of the total measured rotation that occurred as deformation of the purlin web itself rather than rigid-body rotation.
Ratio of web depth to sheet thickness, a slenderness measure that governs web bending and crippling behaviour.
Failure load of the member calculated by a code or analytical method (Cornell, AISI drafts, MBMA proposal, base test method), for comparison with the measured load.
Bending moment capacity of the section computed from code provisions, used as the reference against which the test moment is judged.
Code-based allowable or limiting stress used in capacity calculations for the compression flange, tension flange or web.
Lateral or vertical deflection of the member predicted by analysis at the test load or at the calculated ultimate load.
Effective (reduced) width of the compression flange and effective stiffener length computed by effective-width methods.
Panel-to-member rotational restraint stiffness computed from a mechanical model or code formula, compared against F-test measurements.
Code-computed allowable shear and web crippling strengths of the purlin web at supports.
Pullover strength of a single screw fastener predicted by the biaxial membrane theory developed in the report.
Direction of the applied load relative to the member: uplift (wind suction), gravity, axial, or in-plane shear.
Description of the roof or wall panel and how it is attached to the member (through-fastened screws, standing seam clips), which governs the restraint the panel gives.
Clear span length of each bay of the test assembly between supports, the length over which bending moments develop.
column37: span_ft, l_in [ft (in. in Table I) check]

column2: Number of parallel purlin or girt lines in the test assembly supporting the panel.
Description of any lateral or torsional bracing provided to the member in addition to the panel, such as braces at supports, third points or quarter points.
Number of continuous spans in the tested assembly (single span, three-span continuous, etc.), which controls the moment distribution.
Length of the overlapping splice of purlins at interior supports of continuous assemblies, which strengthens the negative-moment region.
Self weight of the roof or wall assembly per foot of purlin (or per square foot), added to or subtracted from the chamber pressure load.
The applied chamber pressure (or line load) at each intermediate load stage at which gage readings were recorded, giving load-deformation history.
Spacing of the screws attaching the panel to the member flange, which determines how much rotational restraint the panel delivers.
Location and identification of each strain or displacement gage on the specimen, needed to interpret the recorded readings.
column32: sensor, section, position, dim_in [— / in check]

column2: Relative orientation of adjacent purlin lines (same direction, facing or opposed), which affects the system's torsional equilibrium.
Type and thickness of insulation placed between the panel and the member flange, which softens the panel-to-member connection.
Type of standing seam clip connecting the panel to the purlin (sliding two-piece or fixed one-piece), affecting lateral restraint.
The label printed in the report that identifies each individual test specimen or assembly, needed to join the tables of a report.
Designation of which purlin line, span or piece within the assembly a measurement or failure refers to.
Report table, page or hand-calculation from which each summarised value was taken, recorded as provenance rather than a physical quantity.
Which of the two test setups a row belongs to: single-span base test used as the predictor, or three-span confirming test.
Laboratory and calendar date on which the test was run, relevant where several facilities contributed data.
